chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: The decision to go to New York
summary: Musicians encouraged her; she recaps the Pincus search, auditions and the Onyx Club job.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay. Okay, so now we come to the momentous decision that you made to leave Pittsburgh to travel to New York as you told us earlier on in the interview.
You came on the excursion after

Well actually I had been encouraged by a lot of the musicians that would come to the Benjamin Harrison Literary Club because I would think that it was as much as seven or eight months since Gladys Mosier had been at the club. But I was at the Benjamin Literary Club for a year and I saved my money and I decided I was going to take an excursion and come to New York to see what would happen. And that was during the summer of 1937. So Jenny Dillard, the pianist at the club, and I took off this particular summer morning and went for New York.
And you told us about your search for Mr. Pincus, and your auditioning all the way down.
